title: Normalize and persist provider run telemetry
description: Objective: compose raw production provider telemetry with the landed scheduler usage authority at the daemon boundary that can depend on both packages. Deliverable: a focused daemon telemetry adapter/codec/ledger that consumes @moe/runner launch telemetry, runs every usage envelope through @moe/scheduler normalizeUsageMeasurement, preserves upstream versus scheduler refusal provenance, and commits one immutable digest-bound provider-run record for downstream benchmark reads. Hard dependencies: task-5fa25bb33e974f04865b46f9fa0f3910 and task-cbc42f3383444c05a20c6bf56129e8c8; production dispatch consumer is task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9. NOT in scope: launching providers, benchmark statistics, pricing comparison, confirmatory corpus, or claims. Owned paths: focused apps/daemon/src/telemetry/** production/test modules; use existing SqliteEventStore event/decision APIs and no new schema. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: Daemon composition imports only @moe/runner and @moe/scheduler public roots, validates one raw launch-bound telemetry handoff, and delegates every usage envelope in original provider sequence to production normalizeUsageMeasurement without copying its source/coverage matrix.

One frozen canonical provider-run record binds run/effect/attempt, selected and provider-observed model evidence, effort, runtime/profile identities, wall/monotonic timestamps, exact terminal/infra/count/concurrency facts, normalized usage rows, cost-basis metadata, raw receipt digests, and a record digest.

UNKNOWN usage retains quantity null and exact upstream code/layer; PARTIAL retains its measured lower bound; scheduler CONTRACT/MEASUREMENT failures preserve their exact code/layer separately and no client-estimated Claude cost becomes ACTUAL_BILLED.

Existing SqliteEventStore decision/event APIs durably commit exactly one content-bound record; replay is idempotent, changed-byte replay/conflict fails closed, malformed/truncated/digest-mismatched reads return a stable telemetry unreadable code/layer, and no bespoke SQLite schema is added.

Focused real-store tests cover COMPLETE/PARTIAL/UNKNOWN, every declared source with exact non-zero cardinality, lost-ack/reopen and conflict behavior, and mutation-check production coverage plus model/effort bindings.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits 0.
taskRails: Daemon is the direction-safe composition boundary; runner must not depend on scheduler and tests must not inject a fake normalizer.
Preserve upstream provider reason code/layer separately from scheduler CONTRACT/MEASUREMENT code/layer; do not flatten or invent a pass.
No new store schema/table; use public event/decision transactions and strict canonical bytes.
This task lands the durable composition surface; task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 remains the real live dispatch consumer and must be named in the handoff.

implementationPlan.description:
THE FROZEN CANONICAL RECORD (DoD 2). Create `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.ts` and declare the `ProviderRunRecord` interface, every field readonly.

Bind the producer shapes VERBATIM rather than re-deriving them — re-declaring a field the producer already models is the silent-duplicate defect:
- Run/effect/attempt identity: bind `ProviderRunRef` whole (it is exactly `{provider, runRef, effectIntentId, attemptRef, epoch}`), not three hand-rolled id fields.
- Selected AND provider-observed model evidence as TWO SEPARATE fields (`declared` and `observedModel`). A selection is not an observation, and collapsing them destroys the only evidence that the provider ran what was asked for.
- Effort, runtime and profile identities.
- Wall and monotonic timestamps, kept distinct — they answer different questions and a single timestamp field cannot serve both.
- Exact terminal, infrastructure, count-coverage and concurrency facts, typed against the runner's published `ProviderTerminalOutcome`, `ProviderInfrastructureOutcome`, `ProviderCountCoverage`, `ProviderConcurrencyFact`.
- Normalized usage rows typed as the scheduler's `UsageMeasurementRecord` (import `ObservedIntervalRefs` too — without it a consumer can name the record but never construct one).
- Cost-basis metadata, the raw receipt digests, and the record digest.
- TWO SEPARATE provenance fields: the upstream `ProviderTelemetryRefusal {code, layer}` and the scheduler's `LayeredIssue {layer, code}`. Task rail 2 forbids flattening them, and the shape is fixed HERE — if this contract gives them one field, slice 3 cannot comply.

Import every producer type from the `@moe/runner` / `@moe/scheduler` package ROOTS by bare specifier. A deep path fails TS6059 and this repo has no escape hatch.
implementationPlan.note:

TYPECHECK PROVES THE PRODUCER BINDINGS RESOLVE: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` exits 1 with EXACTLY five errors, all of them the step-4 symbols the test imports (PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_CODES, PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS, deriveProviderRunAggregateId, providerRunRefusal, providerRunUnknown). ZERO errors in the record half — every producer type resolved through the BARE package root.

BOUND VERBATIM, NOTHING RE-DERIVED. From @moe/runner: ProviderRunRef (whole — the run/effect/attempt binding, not three hand-rolled ids), ClaudeTelemetryLaunchFacts, ClaudeDeclaredSelection, ClaudeObservedModel, ProviderTerminalOutcome, ProviderInfrastructureOutcome, ClaudeTokenObservations, ClaudeStepObservations, ProviderQuantity, ClaudeTelemetryConcurrency, ProviderText, ProviderTelemetryRefusal. From @moe/scheduler: NormalizedMeasurement, LayeredIssue.

WHERE EACH ENUMERATED DoD-2 FACT LANDS, documented in the file so no sibling re-derives one:
- effort + profile identity: inside `declared` (ClaudeLaunchSelection carries reasoningEffort + profileRevisionId + configuration/policy/orchestration digests). Adding top-level effort/profile fields would have been the silent-duplicate defect.
- runtime identities: `launch`'s runtimeBinding/quotedRuntime/freshRuntime/pinnedClosure digests plus effect/activation/observation.
- selected vs provider-observed model: TWO fields, `declared` and `observedModel`, never defaulted from one another.
- wall interval: `launch.startedAt` / `launch.completedAt`, NOT copied. Monotonic interval is its own field.

THREE DEVIATIONS FROM THE STEP TEXT, each a decision I am disclosing rather than a default:

1. NO top-level `countCoverage: ProviderCountCoverage` field. The runner deliberately WITHHOLDS its `countCoverage` minter from the package root ("Consumers READ handoffs; only this package mints them", claude-surface.ts:160-166), so a run-level roll-up computed here would be the daemon minting a coverage fact the producer refuses to let it mint. ProviderCountCoverage is still bound EXACTLY, transitively and verbatim, as `tokens.coverage` and `steps.coverage`; ProviderConcurrencyFact likewise as `concurrency.fact`.

2. USAGE ROWS ARE `readonly NormalizedMeasurement[]`, NOT `UsageMeasurementRecord[]`. NormalizedMeasurement is published at the scheduler root (index.ts:301-308) and is {measurement, pricebookBinding, truncated, identity} — so this one binding carries DoD 2's "normalized usage rows" AND its "cost-basis metadata" with zero local re-declaration, where a bare UsageMeasurementRecord[] would have forced a parallel cost-basis array whose length could diverge from it. UsageMeasurementRecord and ObservedIntervalRefs are RE-EXPORTED from this module (`export type { ... } from "@moe/scheduler"`) so the closure the plan asked for is intact: a consumer can construct a row from this module alone.

3. SCHEDULER REFUSALS GET A POSITIONED FIELD, `usageRefusals: readonly ProviderRunUsageRefusal[]` where the row is {providerSequence, issues: readonly LayeredIssue[]}. A refused envelope has no measurement, so the scheduler's failure arm cannot carry its own sequence — without providerSequence a silently dropped fourth envelope is byte-identical to a run that only ever emitted three. This keeps the two provenance vocabularies in SEPARATE fields (`upstreamRefusal: ProviderTelemetryRefusal | null` vs `usageRefusals[].issues: LayeredIssue[]`), so slice 3 can comply with task rail 2 without reopening this contract.

DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: a `PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_KEYS` frozen array (the template has one). An interface's keys are not enumerable at runtime, so this slice has no fixture with which to police such a list, and an unpoliced frozen key list drifts from the record silently. It belongs beside the codec in slice 2, where a fixture exists. Recorded for the handoff.

implementationPlan.description:

Include the stable UNREADABLE-RECORD code now, even though slice 1 has no reader for it: slices 2 and 4 both import it, and omitting it forces slice 2 to invent a local one — precisely the duplicate-authority defect this family exists to avoid. Add a frozen layer array so every refusal can name its layer.
- THE NARROW STORE PORT. Name ONLY `commitExpectedVersionDecision`, `getCommandDecision` and the aggregate read slice 4 needs for its replay answer. DO NOT name `commitWithApply` or `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply`. THIS IS THE ONLY SLICE THAT CAN BUILD THIS GUARD — a wide port here hands slice 4 a loaded gun that no test will catch.
- THE DERIVED AGGREGATE ID, bound to the run identity so one provider run is one aggregate head. This is what lets slice 4 borrow conflict detection from the store's expected-version check instead of hand-rolling one.

Run the step-2 tests; they must now pass. Confirm the file is under 250 lines with `grep -c ''` (the template equivalent is 244, so this is a real constraint — if it overruns, split the vocabularies into their own module rather than trimming the record).

The test file's header and imports were updated for the split; it remains ONE suite over the pair, because a code no record field can carry (and the converse) is a defect only a test seeing both halves can catch.

implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILLS (epic rail 6). Every assertion added in step 2 must be proven load-bearing; a green suite is not evidence. For each drill: capture `sha256sum` of the target BEFORE mutating, mutate the PRODUCTION surface, run the focused suite, record which NAMED test reddened and ON WHICH ASSERTION, restore by Edit, then verify the restore by `sha256sum` against the captured hash.

Required drills, each naming the test that must go red:
- D1 VOCABULARY MEMBERSHIP. Remove one member from the reason-code array. The membership test must redden. If the test derives its expected list from the same array it is asserting, it is comparing the array with itself and will stay green — that is the failure this drill exists to expose, and the fix is to pin the names literally while deriving only the COUNT.
- D2 FREEZE. Drop the `Object.freeze` from a vocabulary array. The `Object.isFrozen` assertion must redden.
- D3 AGGREGATE INJECTIVITY. Make the aggregate derivation ignore one identity field (for example, drop `attemptRef` from the input it hashes). The field-by-field injectivity test must redden on THAT field. A derivation silently ignoring a field would let two different runs collide on one aggregate head — which would surface, much later, as slice 4 rejecting a legitimate second run as a conflict.

RESTORE BY sha256, NEVER by `git diff` (blind to untracked paths — every file in this slice is new and untracked, so an empty diff proves nothing) and NEVER by `git checkout` (reverts to HEAD, destroying all of this task's uncommitted work).

A focused vitest run needs `--root .` or it matches ZERO tests and a drill that reddened nothing reads exactly like a drill that found nothing.
implementationPlan.note:
